title: Robust heart rate estimation using wrist-type photoplethysmographic signals during physical exercise: an approach based on adaptive filtering
population: Two datasets of wrist-type PPG records: running subjects, and subjects performing different kinds of arm and forearm movements
findings: PPG signals are easily corrupted by motion artifacts when the subjects perform physical exercise.

Adaptive noise cancellation with accelerometer data followed by an adaptive band-pass filter gave average absolute errors of 1.40 +/- 0.60 bpm on the running dataset and 4.28 +/- 3.16 bpm on the arm and forearm movement dataset.
The method is fully automatic and has an average estimation delay of 0.93 s.
limitations: An algorithm paper on research datasets, using raw PPG and accelerometer signals; the abstract gives no sample size and no device list, and the result does not transfer to a commercial watch's output.
implications: Wrist heart-rate error depends on how the wrist moves, and was larger for varied arm movements than for running; this supports caution on variable-movement runs, not any threshold.
The HQ1 checks do not use the accelerometer and are not a validated artefact detector.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, Physiol Meas 38(2):155-170, published online 5 January 2017, authors Fallet and Vesin. Abstract read in Europe PMC (PMID 28055986); the numbers are copied from it. Sample size is not in the abstract. Design recorded as modelling: an algorithm evaluated on research datasets.
